errors.english: if the community is empowered through the ritual motion
errors.why: What is consecrated (byin gyis brlabs) by the motion-act is the offence, as the next sentence makes explicit, not the community.

note: A sound rendering of a dense Vinaya commentary; the argument about duṣkṛta, adhiṣṭhāna and confessable offences is followed correctly apart from the object of the consecration.

errors.english: that is about to occur one line of text not transcribed
errors.why: The side ends mid-sentence with 'only the cause of the rain that is to occur'; nothing is missing, and the claim of an untranscribed line is spurious.

fix.find: that is about to occur one line of text not transcribed

errors.english: future things are not understood in the same way that form is seen to exist subsequently through the perception of taste as an effect
errors.why: The example is of what is NOT known: that form will exist later as well is not known from perceiving the taste; the English presents it as something that is known.

note: The Pramāṇa argument on inferring causal capacity from taste is mostly tracked correctly; one example is inverted and a false 'missing line' remark is appended.

errors.english: because an identity would absurdly follow through similarity in being an effect and so forth
errors.why: The word begun on the previous side is mi rtag pa nyid, 'impermanence': subject and example would be identical through their similarity in impermanence etc.

fix.find: similarity in being an effect and so forth
fix.replace: similarity in impermanence and so forth

note: A careful rendering of the aviśeṣasama/vikalpasama discussion; only the shared property (impermanence) was misread across the side boundary.

errors.english: because he makes the world joyful by bestowing benefits that were previously absent
errors.why: With the previous side's chos dang bla na, this is 'by benefiting [it] with the Dharma and the unsurpassed (bla na med pa)', not 'benefits previously absent'.

fix.find: by bestowing benefits that were previously absent
fix.replace: by bestowing the Dharma and unsurpassed benefit

errors.english: will come to regard the essence as merely a perception
errors.why: The deluded who cling to life will form the notion that [it] has a core/essence (sāra-saṃjñā), the opposite of reducing essence to a mere perception.

errors.english: which provides the pith instructions of the lineage for the purpose of abandoning
errors.why: rigs here is 'proper/the right means' (instruction on how to abandon), not a lineage.

note: The Four Truths glosses are rendered well, but the opening epithets and the 'empty of the Omniscient One' gloss are misread.

errors.english: whatever does not depend on the essence of something is determined not to have that essence
errors.why: The general principle is that whatever does not depend on something else for its nature is determined (niyata) to that nature; the negation is added.

fix.find: whatever does not depend on the essence of something is determined not to have that essence
fix.replace: whatever does not depend on something else for its nature is determined to that nature

errors.why: It is an example of [a thesis] invalidated BY a pramāṇa (pramāṇa-bādhā), not one that invalidates valid cognition.

note: Lemma-by-lemma commentary on destruction (vināśa) handled reasonably, but the key principle on independence and determination is negated.
Faithful rendering of the pregnant doe episode; the verses are given as prose but without change of sense.

errors.english: You, who possess excellent knowledge, do not desire some specific knowledgeable person.
errors.why: The excellent knowledge belongs to the person the Mīmāṃsaka refuses to accept: 'Why do you not accept someone endowed with excellent knowledge?'

fix.find: You, who possess excellent knowledge, do not desire some specific knowledgeable person.
fix.replace: Why do you not accept someone endowed with excellent knowledge?

errors.english: Even if a single meaning is imagined, it merely follows and conforms to that one desired meaning.
errors.why: gang gis continues the denial: sounds have no fixed nature BY WHICH, even if one meaning were imagined, they would follow only the intended one and others could not be imagined; the English asserts it.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on the Veda's uncertain meaning is broadly followed, but the opening question and one counterfactual are misconstrued.

errors.english: dwelling place filled with glowing embers than one line of text missing or cut off
errors.why: The verse simply continues on the next side; nothing is missing, and the note is spurious.

fix.find: dwelling place filled with glowing embers than one line of text missing or cut off
fix.replace: dwelling place filled with glowing embers than...

errors.english: It would be better to be lifted up and impaled upon a stake
errors.why: The first line ('having everything [one's entrails] drawn out') is not translated.

errors.english: (superior intention) the altruistic resolve of a bodhisattva
errors.why: lhag pa'i bsam pa here is the nāga's earnest resolve in going for refuge; glossing it as a bodhisattva's altruistic resolve is misleading.

note: Good rendering of the Sāgara prophecy and the verses on Saṅgha property, marred by a spurious 'missing line' remark and a dropped half-line.
Accurate rendering of the Madhyamaka objection and reply on 'otherness' as a reason, with speakers and the general/specific reason distinction correctly attributed.

errors.english: The composite nature of hair and so forth is also without purpose.
errors.why: 'dus byas here is saṃskāra in the sense of grooming/adornment of hair and nails (cf. the verses that follow), not 'composite nature'.

note: Faithful rendering of the Bodhicaryāvatāra ch. 8 commentary on the impurity of the body; one technical word misread at the end.
